   394	
   395	## Anti-Stub Rules
   396	
   397	&amp;gt; Stubs that pass quality gates are worse than failing code — they silently ship nothing.
   398	
   399	### Stub Definition
   400	
   401	A **stub** is a function or method whose body consists solely of one or more of:
   402	
   403	1. **`pass`** (possibly preceded by a docstring or logger call)
   404	2. **`raise NotImplementedError(...)`**
   405	3. **Only comments**: `# TODO`, `# FIXME`, `# STUB`, `# placeholder`
   406	4. **Hardcoded defaults with no logic**: `return None`, `return {}`, `return []`, `return ""`, `return 0`, `return False`
   407	5. **Logging-only**: `logger.info(...)` + `pass` or bare `return`
   408	6. **Ellipsis**: `...` as the entire body
   409	
   410	A function that contains conditional logic, calls to domain-specific dependencies, data transformations, or meaningful error handling is **not** a stub, even if parts of it are incomplete.
   411	
   412	### Enforcement by Task Type
   413	
   414	| Task Type | Stubs Allowed? | Notes |
   415	|---|---|---|
   416	| FEATURE | NO | Primary deliverable functions must have real logic |
   417	| REFACTOR | NO | Must contain actual refactored code |
   418	| SCAFFOLDING | CONDITIONAL | Only if AC explicitly permits stubs |
   419	| INFRASTRUCTURE | CONDITIONAL | Only if AC explicitly permits stubs |
   420	| INTEGRATION | NO | Wiring logic must be real |
   421	| DOCUMENTATION | N/A | No deliverable functions |
   422	| TESTING | N/A | No deliverable functions |
   423	
   424	### Primary Deliverable Function
   425	
   426	A primary deliverable function is any function or method that:
   427	
   428	1. Is **named or implied** by the task's acceptance criteria
   429	2. Is the **main entry point** of a module created by the task
   430	3. Is **called by the task's test suite** to exercise core behavior
   431	4. Provides the **core logic** that the task was created to deliver
   432	
   433	Functions that are legitimately thin wrappers (CLI entry points, adapter methods) are NOT stubs.
   434	
   435	### Stub Examples (REJECTED)
   436	
   437	```python
   438	# pass-only stub
   439	async def run_system_plan(description: str, mode: str) -&amp;gt; None:
   440	    logger.info(f"run_system_plan called with {description}")
   441	    pass
   442	
   443	# NotImplementedError stub
   444	def process_payment(order_id: str, amount: float) -&amp;gt; PaymentResult:
   445	    raise NotImplementedError("Payment processing not yet implemented")
   446	
   447	# hardcoded default stub
   448	def get_user_preferences(user_id: str) -&amp;gt; dict:
   449	    return {}
   450	
   451	# TODO-only stub
   452	def validate_input(data: dict) -&amp;gt; ValidationResult:
   453	    # TODO: implement validation logic
   454	    return ValidationResult(valid=True, errors=[])
   455	```
   456	
   457	### Non-Stub Examples (ACCEPTED)
   458	
   459	```python
   460	# Real implementation with logic
   461	async def run_system_plan(description: str, mode: str) -&amp;gt; None:
   462	    detected_mode = detect_mode(description) if mode is None else mode
   463	    questions = generate_questions(detected_mode, description)
   464	    answers = await collect_answers(questions)
   465	    plan = build_plan(detected_mode, answers)
   466	    await write_plan_files(plan)
   467	
   468	# Thin wrapper (NOT a stub — legitimate delegation)
   469	@click.command()
   470	@click.argument("description")
   471	def system_plan(description: str) -&amp;gt; None:
   472	    asyncio.run(run_system_plan(description, mode=None))
   473	```

    16	# Loud synthesis-prompt budget
    17	
    18	Task-work coach bundles reached 109,634 tokens and overflowed the normal checker's
    19	crash-tested 98,304 window (FEAT-8737 TASK-SMOKE-002 turn 1, HTTP 400 receipt in the run
    20	log). The per-tool-result gather cap (GUARDKIT_COACH_GATHER_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS, 12000)
    21	exists but nothing bounds the RENDERED synthesis prompt. Investigate first: which bundle
    22	fields carried the bulk in that receipt's shape. Then enforce an overall budget at the
    23	synthesis-prompt build seam in `guardkit/orchestrator/agent_invoker.py`. Binding spec:
    24	docs/factory-self-fix-scope-and-buildplan.md §2 Fix C + §3.
    25	
    26	## Acceptance Criteria
    27	- [ ] A short investigation note (in the task's implementation summary) names which fields dominated the oversized bundle shape
    28	- [ ] The rendered coach synthesis prompt is bounded by GUARDKIT_COACH_SYNTHESIS_MAX_CHARS (default 300000) — a hermetic test renders an oversized synthetic bundle and asserts the rendered prompt fits the budget
    29	- [ ] Trimming drops bulkiest low-signal content first (raw output tails) and NEVER the verdict-bearing fields (requirements, acceptance criteria, honesty, stub_scan, behavioural_oracle)
    30	- [ ] Trimming is loud: a visible notice inside the prompt names what was cut and by how much, and a WARNING is logged — a hermetic test asserts both
    31	- [ ] A normal-sized bundle renders byte-identically to today (no-trim path proven by test)
    32	- [ ] All modified files pass project-configured lint/format checks with zero errors
    33	
    34	## Implementation Notes
    35	- Chars, not tokens: budget in characters (the seam has no tokenizer); 300000 chars ≈ 85k tokens leaves real margin under 98304.
    36	- This is the permanent fix behind the operator dial used for this very build's run env.</message>
